objects.definition: struct DSU{std::vector<int> par,rnk,sz; int c; explicit DSU(int n):par(n+1),rnk(n+1,0),sz(n+1,1),c(n){for(int i=1;i<=n;++i)par[i]=i;} int find(int i){return par[i]==i?i:par[i]=find(par[i]);} bool same(int i,int j){return find(i)==find(j);} int get_size(int i){return sz[find(i)];} int count()const{return c;} int merge(int i,int j){ if((i=find(i))==(j=find(j))) return -1; else --c; if(rnk[i]>rnk[j]) std::swap(i,j); par[i]=j; sz[j]+=sz[i]; if(rnk[i]==rnk[j]) rnk[j]++; return j; }};
objects.description: Disjoint Set Union (Union-Find) data structure in namespace shah. Manages n elements (1-indexed) supporting path-compressed find, union by rank, component size query, and component count. Constructor DSU(int n) initializes n singleton sets with parents [1..n]. merge(i,j) unions the sets, returning representative id of the merged root or -1 if already in same set; count() returns number of components; same(i,j) tests connectivity; get_size(i) returns size of the component containing i. Indices outside [1..n] are undefined behavior. No dynamic memory beyond std::vectors; lifetime managed by usual C++ object rules.

functions.name: shah::extended_euclid
functions.signature: long long shah::extended_euclid(long long a, long long b, long long& x, long long& y)
functions.description: Computes the extended Euclidean algorithm for integers a and b, returning d = gcd(a, b) and producing coefficients x and y such that a*x + b*y = d. Use it when you need Bezout coefficients (e.g., modular inverses). Runs in O(log min(a,b)). Notes: modifies x and y via references; works for b = 0; for negative inputs, results follow C++ integer division/modulo semantics.
requirements: x and y must be valid lvalue references to long long to receive the output coefficients.
a and b must be representable as long long.
Function may recurse O(log min(a,b)) depth; typical stack limits apply.

functions.name: shah::mod_inverse
functions.signature: long long shah::mod_inverse(long long a, long long m)
functions.description: Computes the modular multiplicative inverse of a modulo m using the extended Euclidean algorithm. Returns a value inv in [0, m-1] such that (a*inv) % m == 1 when gcd(a, m) == 1; returns -1 if the inverse does not exist.
requirements: m must be > 0; modulo by zero or negative modulus leads to undefined behavior.
If gcd(a, m) != 1, the function returns -1; callers must handle this case.
a and m must be representable as long long.

functions.name: shah::power_mod
functions.signature: long long shah::power_mod(long long x, long long n, long long mod)
functions.description: Computes x^n modulo mod using fast exponentiation (binary exponentiation) with 128-bit intermediates to avoid overflow. Intended for non-negative exponents. Runs in O(log n).
requirements: mod must be > 0; the function performs modulo operations and mod == 0 is undefined behavior.
n should be >= 0 to reflect mathematical exponentiation; for n <= 0 the loop does not iterate and the function returns 1 % mod.
x, n, and mod must be representable as long long.

functions.name: shah::z_function
functions.description: Computes the Z-array for string s, where z[i] is the length of the longest substring starting at i that matches the prefix of s. z[0] is 0 by this implementation. Standard linear-time Z-algorithm, O(n). Useful for pattern matching and string processing.
requirements: s can be any valid std::string; no additional preconditions.
Returns a vector<int> of size s.size() with z[0] == 0.

functions.name: shah::DSU::find
functions.description: Finds and returns the representative (root) of the set containing element i, applying path compression for efficiency.
requirements: i must be in the range [1, n] of the DSU constructed by DSU(n); index 0 is not initialized and is invalid.
The DSU object must have been constructed with a size >= i.
Not thread-safe; concurrent calls on the same DSU instance require external synchronization.

functions.name: shah::DSU::same
functions.description: Returns true if elements i and j belong to the same set, false otherwise. Internally calls find on both elements.
requirements: i and j must each be in the range [1, n] of the DSU constructed by DSU(n).
The DSU object must have been constructed with size >= max(i, j).
Not thread-safe; concurrent calls on the same DSU instance require external synchronization.

functions.name: shah::DSU::get_size
functions.description: Returns the size (number of elements) of the set containing element i.
requirements: i must be in the range [1, n] of the DSU constructed by DSU(n).
The DSU object must have been constructed with size >= i.
Not thread-safe; concurrent calls on the same DSU instance require external synchronization.

functions.name: shah::DSU::count
functions.description: Returns the current number of disjoint sets being tracked by the DSU.
requirements: The DSU must have been constructed; no additional preconditions.
Value decreases by one on each successful merge of two distinct sets.

functions.name: shah::DSU::merge
functions.description: Unites the sets containing i and j using union by rank and updates sizes. If i and j are already in the same set, returns -1. Otherwise, returns the representative of the merged set and decreases the component count.
requirements: i and j must each be in the range [1, n] of the DSU constructed by DSU(n).
The DSU object must have been constructed with size >= max(i, j).
Caller should handle the return value -1 as 'no-op because elements were already in the same set'.
Not thread-safe; concurrent calls on the same DSU instance require external synchronization.

data_types.description: Any sequence of bytes representable in a std::string. No specific encoding or structure is required; may contain ASCII, UTF-8, binary NULs, or any arbitrary characters. Used as generic string data for string-processing algorithms.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate interesting arbitrary strings to exercise shah::z_function.
# Goals:
# - Cover empty, single-char, repeated patterns, borders, partial repeats, random, unicode-like bytes, with and without NULs.
# - Keep under 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic given seed, but include variety per call.

MAX_LEN = 2048

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Include full byte range to allow NULs and non-ASCII
    return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))

def _repeat_pattern(rng: random.Random, base: bytes, min_rep: int = 1, max_rep: int = 64) -> bytes:
    reps = rng.randint(min_rep, max_rep)
    return base * reps

def _make_border_string(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct s = P + X + P where P is a non-empty prefix that reappears, to create non-trivial Z-values
    # Choose P
    plen = rng.randint(1, 64)
    P_type = rng.choice(['alpha', 'alnum', 'bytes'])
    if P_type == 'alpha':
        P = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(plen)).encode('utf-8')
    elif P_type == 'alnum':
        P = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(plen)).encode('utf-8')
    else:
        P = _rand_bytes(rng, plen)
    # X is a small differing middle to avoid full match, but sometimes empty to create full periodicity
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        X = b''
    else:
        # ensure X differs at least at first byte from following P[0] with high probability
        if len(P) > 0:
            b0 = (P[0] + 1) % 256
        else:
            b0 = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        X = bytes([b0]) + _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 16))
    return P + X + P

def _make_periodic_string(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # s is made by repeating a small base; z-function has large z values at multiples of period
    base_len = rng.randint(1, 64)
    base = _rand_bytes(rng, base_len)
    s = _repeat_pattern(rng, base, min_rep=2, max_rep=64)
    # Optionally truncate or append tail to break last period
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        tail = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, base_len - 1 if base_len > 1 else 0))
        s += tail
    return s

def _make_prefix_suffix_overlap(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # s = A + B where B shares a long prefix with A's prefix but differs at next char
    a_len = rng.randint(2, 128)
    A = _rand_bytes(rng, a_len)
    # Choose overlap length
    k = rng.randint(1, a_len - 1)
    B = bytearray(A[:k])
    # Ensure next char mismatches if we add one
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        next_byte = (A[k] + 1) % 256 if k < len(A) else rng.randrange(0, 256)
        B.append(next_byte)
    # Optional random tail
    B.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 32)))
    return bytes(A + B)

def _make_random_unicode_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII, multi-byte UTF-8 sequences, and NULs
    out = bytearray()
    length = rng.randint(1, 1024)
    while len(out) < length:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.5:
            out.append(rng.choice(b" \t\n\r\x00" + bytes(string.printable, 'ascii')))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            # 2-byte UTF-8
            cp = rng.randint(0x80, 0x7FF)
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
        elif choice < 0.95:
            # 3-byte UTF-8
            cp = rng.randint(0x800, 0xFFFF)
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                cp = 0xE000
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            # 4-byte UTF-8
            cp = rng.randint(0x10000, 0x10FFFF)
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
    return bytes(out[:length])

def _make_edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Deterministic set of classic Z-algorithm trigger strings
    cases = []
    cases.append(b"")
    cases.append(b"a")
    cases.append(b"aaaaaa")
    cases.append(b"abababababab")
    cases.append(b"abcababcababcabx")
    cases.append(b"mississippi")
    cases.append(b"aaaaaabaaaaaa")
    cases.append(b"\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00")
    cases.append(b"\x00abc\x00abc\x01")
    cases.append(b"banana$")
    cases.append(b"abcabcabcd")
    cases.append(b"abcdabca")
    return cases

def _assemble(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose a strategy
    strategies = [
        lambda: _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 1024)),
        lambda: _make_periodic_string(rng),
        lambda: _make_border_string(rng),
        lambda: _make_prefix_suffix_overlap(rng),
        lambda: _make_random_unicode_like(rng),
    ]

    # Sometimes concatenate multiple segments to create composite structures
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # pick from curated edge cases directly
        parts.append(rng.choice(_make_edge_cases(rng)))
    # Add 1-3 strategy parts
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        parts.append(rng.choice(strategies)())
    # Optionally insert delimiters/pattern breakers
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        delim_choices = [b"\x00", b"#", b"$", b"\n", b"\xff\x00\xff"]
        parts.insert(rng.randrange(0, len(parts)+1), rng.choice(delim_choices) * rng.randint(1, 8))
    s = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure not too long
    if len(s) > MAX_LEN:
        s = s[:MAX_LEN]
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    data = _assemble(rng)
    # Guarantee non-empty sometimes, but allow empty too for coverage
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        data = b""
    # Final cap
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
